model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, LoRA adapter trained 200 steps on 6 tables (templated questions), Q4_K_M GGUF via llama.cpp
test: 100 verified questions about an UNSEEN table (penguins) in SHAPES never used in training: two conditions, BETWEEN, DISTINCT, HAVING, GROUP BY AVG, top-3 (tinyforge data tabular --hard)
reading: No meaningful gain: tuned 98% vs the same base told to reply with SQL only 97% (n=100, difference is noise). On the easy templated test the gap was 100% vs 93% (7 malformed MAX calls). For an 8B instruct model, fine-tuning on templated SQL mostly fixes output consistency; it does not add capability it already had. Contrast: Qwen2.5-3B on titanic scored 98% tuned vs 70% instructed base (benchmarks/e2e-titanic-3b-soup.json).
caveats: n=100, one run, greedy decoding, no confidence interval
misses on both sides are column-selection mistakes in GROUP BY queries (e.g. dropping the group column)
tuned and base share the same Q4_K_M weights: the only difference is the LoRA scale (1.0 vs 0.0)
